title: For Change-O, TIgGER and SCOPer
body: Keep full. Between them these tools read the IMGT-gapped sequence_alignment and germline_alignment, the junction and junction_length, the germline coordinates ( v_germline_start ...) and the N-region lengths (np1_length, np2_length): only full has them all. It also has airr_assembly_status, to keep the complete rows before clonal analysis. v_call lists the alleles that match a read equally well after the call, comma-separated, as TIgGER and Change-O expect. More on Coming from Immcantation.

title: Name your own columns
body: A comma-separated list writes exactly those columns, in that order. A name AlignAIR does not know is written as an empty column, so check the spelling. A list that names no junction, alignment, region or identity column (nor vj_in_frame or stop_codon) skips the AIRR assembly, as minimal does.

title: The run record beside the table
body: Each command-line run also writes out.tsv.run.json: the model's id, version and checksum, the fingerprints of the germline set the calls came from (yours, with --reference), the genotype, the options, and the counts of complete, partial and failed rows. Keep it with the table for your methods section. --no-run-metadata leaves it out.

title: Reading the T/F columns
body: productive, rev_comp, vj_in_frame, stop_codon and segmentation_low_quality hold the AIRR strings T and F; an empty cell means unknown, not false. length_cropped is T or empty, and empty means the read was not cut. pandas reads them as strings, so compare with "T", never with .astype(bool), which turns "F" into True:

title: Run at scale
body: Use a GPU or every CPU core, keep memory flat on large files, and align many samples in a loop or in nf-core/airrflow.

title: On a GPU
body: --device auto, the default, uses an NVIDIA GPU (CUDA) when there is one, else Apple's GPU (MPS), else the CPU; alignair doctor shows which as device_auto. Name a device with --device cuda, cuda:1, mps or cpu. On a GPU, reads go in batches of 256; raise --batch-size on a large GPU, lower it if the GPU runs out of memory. A GPU and the CPU give the same calls and junctions, but their arithmetic differs in the last digits: on the example reads, mutation_rate differs by up to 0.00001, and on a short fragment a candidate set ( v_call_set) can differ. The run record (out.tsv.run.json) keeps the device each run used.

title: On the CPU: --threads
body: Without --threads, one process runs, with batches of 64 reads, on PyTorch's default number of threads: one per physical core of the machine, or of the CPUs the job is bound to. On a shared node whose scheduler does not bind jobs to their CPUs, that is more cores than your job was given. --threads N runs N worker processes of one thread each, with batches of 16 reads per worker; this scales better than one process using many threads. Set N to the cores your job was given (on SLURM, $SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK), and leave some free on a shared desktop. On a GPU, --threads only sets the CPU threads of the one process. Worker processes are a command-line feature: in Python, one process predicts. On a CPU cluster, the command line with --threads suits large samples; the Python loop, which loads the model once, suits many small ones (a command-line run of 20 reads takes about 2 s, start-up and model load included).

title: Speed and memory on the CPU
body: To size a job on a CPU cluster or an HPC node: the throughput (reads per second) and peak memory of each setting, measured on 24,000 simulated IGH reads of about 380 nt, on the CPU of an 8-core desktop (Intel i7-10700F, 16 threads, with other jobs running; a range is of two runs): --threads 1, "113", "1.3 GB"], [--threads 4, "250", "1.6 GB"], [--threads 8, "340 to 415", "2.2 GB"], ] /> So with --threads 8, a million reads take 40 to 50 minutes on such a machine. TRB contigs of about 350 nt ran at much the same speed. Memory is for the default chunk of 20,000 reads, the model included; it does not grow with the file. Ask a scheduler for 4 GB with 8 threads.

title: Large files in constant memory
body: The command line streams its input: it reads 20,000 reads at a time (--chunk-size), aligns and writes them, then reads the next chunk. Memory depends on the chunk and batch sizes and the number of workers, not on the size of the file (only the read ids are remembered, to rename repeats); the figures are above. The table is written to a temporary file and moved into place when the run ends, so a run that stops halfway leaves no half-written table. --columns minimal skips the AIRR assembly and writes much smaller rows, when the calls are all you need (Choose output columns).

title: Many samples
body: Run one command per sample. Download the model once before you start, and run the jobs with --offline, so parallel jobs never fetch it at the same time; --quiet drops the update notice. With a tab-separated manifest whose columns are sample and input: Each command-line run loads the model again; for many small samples, the Python loop loads it once. Each run of the command line writes its sample's own .run.json. To give each table its sample's id, see A sample id for every row.

title: A SLURM job array
body: On a cluster, run one job per sample. With the same manifest, this script aligns the sample on line $SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID + 1 (line 1 is the header) on the cores the job was given: Keep --threads equal to --cpus-per-task, and set --array to 1- the number of samples. Download the model once on a node with internet, into the cache every job reads (ALIGNAIR_CACHE_DIR on a shared disk), then submit: 4 GB and two hours cover a sample of a million reads at the speeds measured above; scale them to your samples.

title: Apptainer or Singularity
body: Clusters that do not run Docker usually run Apptainer (Singularity), which runs the Docker image as it is. Pull it once into a file, then put apptainer exec alignair.sif before any command on these pages: Apptainer runs as you, with your home directory mounted, so the model is cached in your own ~/.cache/alignair (or ALIGNAIR_CACHE_DIR), and the image runs on the CPU. With Singularity, write singularity for apptainer.

title: nf-core/airrflow
body: airrflow takes AlignAIR's tables in its assembled mode, one per sample, listed in the samplesheet's filename column. Its other required columns (subject, species, tissue, locus and more) are listed in airrflow's usage docs: check them for the version you run. On an AIRR table, airrflow re-assigns the genes by default (--reassign, default true), which replaces AlignAIR's calls. Pass --reassign false to keep them. airrflow's later steps look calls up in its own germline set, IMGT's by default ( --reference_fasta, on its parameters page). The IG models write OGRDB names, which that set does not hold: check how your airrflow version uses its germline set before you rely on those steps.

text: alignair genotype: the share of a gene's single-allele rows its alleles explain (default 0.875)

title: --min-reads
text: alignair genotype: the single-allele rows a gene needs to be genotyped (default 10)

title: --debug
text: alignair genotype: include the full exception traceback on errors

title: --error-format
text: alignair genotype: runtime error format on stderr (default: text)

title: sequence_id
text: The read's id: the input record's id (a repeated id gets a _dupN suffix), or the --id-column value of a table.

title: sequence
text: The read as aligned (cut to its first 575 nt when longer); for a reverse-complement read, the original read (see rev_comp).

title: rev_comp
text: T when the read was reverse-complemented to align: coordinates and alignments then refer to the reverse complement of sequence.

title: locus
text: The locus of the V call (IGH, IGK, IGL, TRA, TRB, TRD or TRG); a model of one locus writes it for every read.

title: v_call
text: The V allele call; alleles that match the read equally well follow it, comma-separated (IgBLAST's convention).

title: d_call
text: The D allele call: one allele (only v_call lists tied alleles).

title: j_call
text: The J allele call: one allele (only v_call lists tied alleles).

title: c_call
text: The constant-region gene. AlignAIR does not call it; a --metadata table may fill it (10x c_gene).

title: productive
text: T when the rearrangement is productive: V and J in frame, no stop codon, conserved junction anchors.

title: productive_prediction
text: The same call as productive, kept for tools that read this column.

title: vj_in_frame
text: T when V and J are in the same reading frame.

title: stop_codon
text: T when the aligned sequence holds a stop codon in the V reading frame.

title: v_identity
text: The fraction of the aligned V bases that match the germline.

title: d_identity
text: The fraction of the aligned D bases that match the germline.

title: j_identity
text: The fraction of the aligned J bases that match the germline.

title: sequence_alignment
text: The aligned read, IMGT-gapped (dots in the V gaps).

title: germline_alignment
text: The germline the read aligns to, IMGT-gapped, position for position with sequence_alignment, N in the untemplated bases (np1, np2).

title: junction
text: The junction: CDR3 with its conserved anchors (V's Cys to J's Trp or Phe).

title: junction_aa
text: The junction translated (X for an incomplete codon).

title: junction_aa_length
text: The junction's length in amino acids.

title: np1
text: The untemplated bases between V and D; without a D call (a D too short to call included), all the bases between V and J.

title: np2
text: The untemplated bases between D and J; empty without a D call.

title: v_cigar
text: The V alignment of the read against its germline, as a CIGAR string over the whole read: S for the read before V, N for the germline bases b

title: d_cigar
text: The D alignment of the read against its germline, as a CIGAR string over the whole read: S for the read before D, N for the germline bases b

title: j_cigar
text: The J alignment of the read against its germline, as a CIGAR string over the whole read: S for the read before J, N for the germline bases b

title: v_sequence_start
text: Where V starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T).

title: v_sequence_end
text: Where V ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T).

title: v_germline_start
text: Where the V part of sequence_alignment starts in the IMGT-gapped V germline: 1, as the alignment starts at the germline's first position, wi

title: v_germline_end
text: Where the V alignment ends in the IMGT-gapped V germline, its gaps counted, as Change-O counts it. Empty for a row without the alignment.

title: d_sequence_start
text: Where D starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T).

title: d_sequence_end
text: Where D ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T).

title: d_germline_start
text: Where the alignment starts in the D germline.

title: d_germline_end
text: Where the alignment ends in the D germline.

title: j_sequence_start
text: Where J starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T).

title: j_sequence_end
text: Where J ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T).

title: j_germline_start
text: Where the alignment starts in the J germline.

title: j_germline_end
text: Where the alignment ends in the J germline.

title: fwr1_start
text: Where the framework region 1 starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its first read base.

title: fwr1_end
text: Where the framework region 1 ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its last read base.

title: cdr1_start
text: Where the CDR1 starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its first read base.

title: cdr1_end
text: Where the CDR1 ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its last read base.

title: fwr2_start
text: Where the framework region 2 starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its first read base.

title: fwr2_end
text: Where the framework region 2 ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its last read base.

title: cdr2_start
text: Where the CDR2 starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its first read base.

title: cdr2_end
text: Where the CDR2 ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its last read base.

title: fwr3_start
text: Where the framework region 3 starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its first read base.

title: fwr3_end
text: Where the framework region 3 ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its last read base.

title: cdr3_start
text: Where the CDR3 starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its first read base.

title: cdr3_end
text: Where the CDR3 ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its last read base.

title: fwr4
text: The read's framework region 4: IMGT's FR4, from the J's Trp or Phe codon (the junction's last codon) to the end of the J.

title: fwr4_start
text: Where the framework region 4 starts in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its first read base.

title: fwr4_end
text: Where the framework region 4 ends in sequence (in its reverse complement when rev_comp is T): its last read base.

title: v_sequence_alignment
text: The read's V part of sequence_alignment.

title: v_germline_alignment
text: The V germline's part of germline_alignment.

title: v_alignment_start
text: Where V starts in sequence_alignment and germline_alignment.

title: v_alignment_end
text: Where V ends in sequence_alignment and germline_alignment.

title: d_sequence_alignment
text: The read's D part of sequence_alignment.

title: d_germline_alignment
text: The D germline's part of germline_alignment.

title: d_alignment_start
text: Where D starts in sequence_alignment and germline_alignment.

title: d_alignment_end
text: Where D ends in sequence_alignment and germline_alignment.

title: j_sequence_alignment
text: The read's J part of sequence_alignment.

title: j_germline_alignment
text: The J germline's part of germline_alignment.

title: j_alignment_start
text: Where J starts in sequence_alignment and germline_alignment.

title: j_alignment_end
text: Where J ends in sequence_alignment and germline_alignment.

title: v_call_set
text: The candidate set: the V alleles the model scored as possible before the germline refinement, comma-separated (the v_call can fall outside i

title: d_call_set
text: The candidate set: the D alleles the model scored as possible before the germline refinement, comma-separated (the d_call can fall outside i

title: j_call_set
text: The candidate set: the J alleles the model scored as possible before the germline refinement, comma-separated (the j_call can fall outside i

title: mutation_rate
text: AlignAIR's estimate of the read's somatic mutation rate over its V, D and J.

title: orientation
text: How the read was turned to align: forward, reverse_complement, complement or reverse.

title: input_sequence
text: The read as given, before orientation.

title: segmentation_low_quality
text: T when the read's V or J segment came out empty or reversed: treat its calls with caution.

title: length_cropped
text: T when the read was longer than 575 nt and only its first 575 nt were aligned; a row cut inside its J is partial (j_cropped).

title: airr_assembly_status
text: complete (every field derived), partial (some fields left blank, or calls that rest on part of the read: see airr_assembly_reason) or failed

title: airr_assembly_reason
text: Why a partial row is partial: no_v (the read has no V call), nonproductive_indel, missing_calls_or_coordinates, collapsed_segment, incomplet

title: airr_assembly_error
text: The error that stopped a failed row's assembly.

title: ALIGNAIR_AIRR_ASSEMBLY_FAILED
text: AIRR assembly failed for one record. Carries the record identifier and the originating error so an unexpected (non-data) failure surfaces wi

title: ALIGNAIR_ARTIFACT_INTEGRITY_FAILED
text: Artifact bytes or bound identities failed verification.

title: ALIGNAIR_CONFIG_INVALID
text: A training request is invalid (bad hyperparameters / config / reference). Raised *before* the full model is allocated so misuse fails fast w

title: ALIGNAIR_DATA_INVALID
text: A record, batch, or component violated its declared data contract.

title: ALIGNAIR_DEPENDENCY_MISSING
text: A requested feature needs an optional dependency.

title: ALIGNAIR_DOWNLOAD_INTEGRITY_FAILED
text: A downloaded artifact failed SHA256 verification.

title: ALIGNAIR_ERROR
text: Base for classified AlignAIR failures; built-in compatibility is added by subclasses.

title: ALIGNAIR_GENOTYPE_ALLELE_NOT_FOUND
text: A genotype names alleles the reference does not hold; their sequences belong in the reference.

title: ALIGNAIR_INPUT_INVALID
text: Invalid user input or sequence data.

title: ALIGNAIR_INTERNAL_ERROR
text: Unexpected defect, classified only at an application boundary.

title: ALIGNAIR_INTERRUPTED
text: An application operation was interrupted by the user.

title: ALIGNAIR_IO_FAILED
text: An expected filesystem or operating-system operation failed.

title: ALIGNAIR_METADATA_ID_INVALID
text: A metadata join key occurs more than once; neither row may silently win.

title: ALIGNAIR_MODEL_INTEGRITY_FAILED
text: A model section failed verification (also catchable as ValueError).

title: ALIGNAIR_MODEL_INVALID
text: A model artifact is missing, incompatible, or unusable.

title: ALIGNAIR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND
text: No such model: a model file that does not exist, an id no registry lists, a hub repo, revision or file that is not there.

title: ALIGNAIR_MODEL_SECTION_MISSING
text: A required model section is absent (also catchable as KeyError).

title: ALIGNAIR_MODEL_UNAVAILABLE
text: A fetch was needed while offline: the model is not available from the cache. Not retryable: the same call fails the same way until offline m

title: ALIGNAIR_NUMERICS_INVALID
text: Non-finite model outputs, losses, or gradients.

title: ALIGNAIR_PREDICTION_COUNT_MISMATCH
text: The writer was given a different number of ids / sequences / predictions — a pipeline or model defect. Raised instead of silently truncating

title: ALIGNAIR_REGISTRY_FAILED
text: Model registry lookup or transfer failed; ``retryable`` says whether a retry may succeed.

title: ALIGNAIR_REGISTRY_INVALID
text: A registry's catalog cannot be used: not JSON, no models mapping, a malformed entry, a version that fails validation.

title: ALIGNAIR_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE
text: A registry source or the hub could not be reached or read (the network, a server, a local registry that is not there). Retryable unless the

title: ALIGNAIR_TRAINING_DATA_INVALID
text: Simulator or training records lack the fields needed to construct targets.

title: ALIGNAIR_TRAINING_NUMERICS_INVALID
text: Loss or a gradient became NaN/Inf — training is aborted with a per-task diagnostic rather than continuing to corrupt the weights.
